subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In the 1960s, civil rights activists organized freedom rides to challenge segregation.
• Activists rode buses from Washington, D.C., to New Orleans, Louisiana.
• This freedom ride began on May 4, 1961, and ended on May 17, 1961.
• Activists rode buses from Nashville, Tennessee, to Birmingham, Alabama.
• This freedom ride began on May 20, 1961, and ended on May 24, 1961.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the order in which the two freedom rides occurred. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: In the 1960s, civil rights activists in different regions organized freedom rides to challenge segregation.
choices.B: A freedom ride from Nashville, Tennessee, to Birmingham, Alabama, was followed by one from Washington, D.C., to New Orleans, Louisiana.
choices.C: After activists rode buses from Washington, D.C., to New Orleans, activists rode buses from Nashville, Tennessee, to Birmingham, Alabama.
choices.D: From May 4 to May 17, 1961, activists rode buses from Washington, D.C., to New Orleans, Louisiana.

explanation:
Choice C is correct. It emphasizes chronological order: the Nashville freedom ride (May 20-24, 1961) occurred after the Washington to New Orleans ride (May 4-17, 1961).

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. While the sentence does emphasize the order in which the two freedom rides occurred, the order is incorrect. The Washington, D.C., ride took place from May 4 to May 17, 1961, which was before the Nashville ride (May 20-24, 1961).
